question: How did he build the wearable that gives directions through vibration?
reference_answer: Haptic Atlas is the v1 wearable of the cross-university haptic navigation research program run with Columbia GSAPP and Tsinghua SoA. It runs Python and microcontroller firmware, driving a GIS → routing → vibration pipeline built over NYC APS (accessible pedestrian signals) data and custom data. The approach was to move the route off the screen and onto the body, mapping live map and geo data to real-time vibrotactile cues so that direction and proximity arrive as sensation rather than as something to be read. His role is listed as Project Lead, with instructor Daniel Leithinger, running Aug 2024 to present.
